Its success branch and activity write the execution and accepted result without diagnostic rows.             Evidence: Contract counterexample, not executed product code: a reviewer exits successfully with valid actual model/effort and a valid verdict, but the CLI supplies no input/output token counts.             R4-F02 - A fast artifact-review exit with missing provenance has no consistent execution-identity path. Severity medium. Classification: implementer edit.

            Location: docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture-Amendment-1-Durable-HV.md:1653; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture-Amendment-1-Durable-HV.md:1654; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture-Amendment-1-Durable-HV.md:1655; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture-Amendment-1-Durable-HV.md:1656; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture-Amendment-1-Durable-HV.md:1753; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture-Amendment-1-Durable-HV.md:1769; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture-Amendment-1-Durable-HV.md:3285; FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-003 criteria 1, 2, 4.

            Defect: The added missing-provenance failure forbids an execution row and puts the launch identity in a diagnostic, but the canonical DTO, field writers and relationship still promise one execution per launched process. For an exit before first renewal, Complete writes Attempt.ExecutionId only when Outcome.execution is set, and that same branch always writes the execution row. There is no declared representation that both honors the no-row rule and sets the promised attempt identity.

            Evidence: Contract counterexample: an adapter has a provenance source and launches, but a short run exits before RenewalInterval with no readable actual model or effort. The pre-launch guard cannot catch this history. Line 1655 explicitly selects runtime_identity_unavailable with no execution row. Leaving Outcome.execution null skips both the row and Attempt.ExecutionId at 1753; supplying metadata creates the forbidden row and cannot truthfully supply mandatory actual model/effort. The failure activity at 1769 instead says record the execution whenever a process started. B.9 labels the relationship one per launched process. The ID in a diagnostic is useful evidence but is not the specified writer of Attempt.ExecutionId.

            Change to PASS: Define one canonical representation for launched-but-unverifiable execution. Separate the observed launch identity and times from optional validated provenance, or explicitly specify an equivalent non-fabricating contract. Give fast completion an independent writer for Attempt.ExecutionId; state consistently whether an execution row is absent and how that exception relates to the nullable relationship. Update the DTO, producer, Complete activity, storage prose and B.9. Extend HostileReviewFastExitRecordsExecutionAndTerminalFields with launch-then-missing-provenance before the first renewal, and retain truthful diagnostics. Record the named cases on the existing TEST in approved H0, bind in H3; no new operator policy is needed.

            Affected claims: AM2, AM3, AM9, AM13.

            R4-F04 - Claim-time reassignment promises capacity filtering that the canonical round-robin policy cannot perform. Severity medium. Classification: implementer edit.

            Location: docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture-Amendment-1-Durable-HV.md:962; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture-Amendment-1-Durable-HV.md:977; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture-Amendment-1-Durable-HV.md:978; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture-Amendment-1-Durable-HV.md:981; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture-Amendment-1-Durable-HV.md:1328; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture-Amendment-1-Durable-HV.md:1343; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture-Amendment-1-Durable-HV.md:1347; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture-Amendment-1-Durable-HV.md:1352; FR-MCP-HVPIPE-002; FR-MCP-HVPIPE-007.

            Defect: ClaimHvRunCommand asks RoundRobinAssignment for an eligible reviewer with free capacity, but HvReviewerEligibility deliberately excludes capacity and RoundRobinAssignment selects and advances the cursor for the first eligible reviewer. Its only inputs are submitter/author identity, and its only refusal is no eligible reviewer. It has no claim-time candidate predicate or capacity branch. The caller and canonical shared policy specify different selections.

            Evidence: Contract counterexample: a queued request loses its assignee to Offline. After the cursor, reviewer A is Online and eligible but at MaxConcurrentRuns; later reviewer B is Online, eligible and free. RoundRobinAssignment at 1343/1352 returns A and writes its cursor. Claim at 962/978 promises B or a truthful no-capacity result. Starting A exceeds capacity; rejecting A and rolling back can choose A again on every poll and starve B, especially because A has no review time limit. Repeated committed cursor skips are another unspecified algorithm and contradict null/writes-nothing at 962. SerializableWrite provides isolation but does not supply the missing selection rule.

            Change to PASS: Define capacity-aware claim reassignment in the one canonical round-robin contract, with an explicit mode or caller-provided candidate filter, and atomically recheck capacity with the claim. Preserve admission eligibility and admission while all reviewers are busy. Specify cursor/request behavior when no capacity exists. Propagate the unit, policy, activity and test catalog. Add named cases to existing FR/TR/TEST-MCP-HVPIPE-002 or -007 for skipping a full eligible reviewer when a later one is free, and all-full with no spurious write; H0 mocks, H3 production.

            Affected claims: AM2, AM3.

          - Line 2813 requires ModelGradeDisagreeVerdictPassingScoresRefusedVerdictMatch, but neither check 5 nor the per-response grades schema at line 3718 contains the predicate or per-entry verdict semantics needed to produce that refusal. Define per-response verdict semantics and the batch overall verdict, validate their consistency with scores/findings, and make the named negative test match that rule without preventing legitimate failing grades or mixed ranges from being recorded.


          Classification: Implementer edit. Operator decision: none. Live identity comparison is present, but missing evidence can still pass; the required verdict negative case has no defined acceptance rule.


          ### AR1-F9: Single-turn transaction scope still includes a shared session write


          Location: docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:152; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:292; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:332; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:2125.


          The locked turn-level decision isolates the turn and moves the session summary to a separate post-commit write. The shared SerializableWrite definition and Phase B write contract still read and write the common session row inside every single-turn transaction while promising different turns never conflict.


          - Two different turns in one session address the same session row under the stated Serializable delegate. Concurrent updates to that shared row require serialization and can consume the same bounded transient-conflict retries the architecture exposes as 409.


          - Line 152 explicitly makes summary refresh a separate write whose failure cannot fail the turn. Lines 332 and 2125 do not identify any other permitted session-row mutation or reconcile their in-transaction write with that decision.


          Change required: Make the one shared transaction contract match the locked decision: locate/validate the parent as needed, but mutate only the target turn and its children inside a single-turn transaction; specify the session summary update as a separate post-commit operation with its own non-failing outcome. Define the provider-specific locking/read strategy and test concurrent writes to different turns plus a failed summary refresh.


          Classification: Implementer edit. Operator decision: none. The round-5 turn-level reconciliation was not propagated consistently into the shared component and review units.

          ---

          # Stateless Agent Context Management

          ## Summary

          Create `docs/Stateless-Agent-Context-Management.md` as the decision-complete BDPv4 plan for stateless agent requests.

          Each invocation receives a bounded, reproducible package containing the current request, canonical operator profile and rules, applicable requirements, related session-log evidence, trusted prior responses, and relevant current-commit code. Conversation history is not carried forward.

          ## Architecture

          - Store packages, responses, grades, and relationships in the relational store as authoritative records.

          - Project response artifacts into GraphRAG for semantic retrieval while retaining deterministic relational fallback.

          - Record source hashes, commit identity, selection rationale, token usage, contradictions, blockers, and omitted candidates.

          - Fail explicitly when mandatory context exceeds the token budget.

          - Grade every response through deterministic evidence checks and an independent model.

          - Require correctness and completeness of at least 98 percent with zero FAIL or UNKNOWN before trusting a response.

          - Preserve rejected and stale responses for audit while excluding them from trusted retrieval.

          - Support `implements`, `verifies`, `depends_on`, `supports`, `contradicts`, `supersedes`, `blocks`, `derived_from`, and `relevant_to` relationships.

          - Introduce an opt-in `Mcp:AgentContext` mode while retaining the current stateful behavior during the pilot.

          ## BDPv4 Implementation Plan

          1. Register requirements, use cases, acceptance criteria, and public interface contracts.

          2. Establish green discriminating mock tests with negative controls before production implementation.

          3. Add authoritative storage for packages, responses, grades, and graph relationships.

          4. Implement deterministic package construction from requirements, profile, rules, session logs, TODOs, code, receipts, and prior responses.

          5. Implement independent grading, acceptance, staleness, rejection, and supersession.

          6. Add GraphRAG projection with deterministic fallback.

          7. Expose REST, MCP, client, REPL, and plugin interfaces.

          8. Pilot stateless execution against the current stateful workflow before changing defaults.

          Tests cover deterministic replay, mandatory profile completeness, ranking, contradictions, grading thresholds, stale dependencies, workspace isolation, secret exclusion, token overflow, GraphRAG fallback, concurrency, idempotency, and the full zero-failure, zero-skip suite.

          ## Commit and Push

          - Preserve the primary checkout, which has 153 unrelated dirty paths and is behind `origin/develop`.

          - Fetch current `origin/develop`.

          - Create an isolated worktree and temporary branch from the fetched remote commit.

          - Write only `docs/Stateless-Agent-Context-Management.md`.

          - Validate the document with `git diff --check`, heading checks, secret inspection, and an on-disk readback.

          - Commit with `docs: plan stateless agent context management`.

          - Fetch `origin/develop` again immediately before publishing.

          - Rebase the single-file commit if the remote advanced.

          - Push with `git push origin HEAD:develop`.

          - Verify the remote `develop` SHA equals the new commit and inspect the remote commit's file list.

          - Stop and report the exact error if branch protection or a non-fast-forward update rejects the push. Do not force-push or substitute a pull request.

          - Retain the isolated worktree and branch after the push. Do not delete them without explicit authorization.

          Defect: BuildPackage returns 200 for any identical saved package, including Overflow, while the invocation process treats every 200/201 as a usable package and invokes the model. The mandatory fail-the-invocation decision is therefore not invariant under retry.

          FAIL; Implementer edit; claims M1, M2, M5.

          Defect: The server-computed hash and the submitted hash have different required meanings, but only one Sha256 is stored. Submission overwrites it with the server hash, so the later deterministic grade cannot identify a submitted mismatch.


          - Evidence: Section 6.3 explicitly requires a submitted hash that differs from the source to make the deterministic evidence check FAIL.

          - Evidence: AgentResponseEvidenceEntity has only Sha256 and CommitSha. Submit computes source hashes and saves evidence with those hashes. There is no submitted-hash field, immutable submission snapshot, or persisted mismatch finding. SubmissionSha256 is an irreversible fingerprint, not the missing input.

          - Evidence: Counterexample: cite an existing file with deliberately wrong hash Hbad. Submission stores Hactual. After restart the grade compares Hactual with the file and cannot distinguish this submission from one that cited Hactual.


          Specific change to PASS: Retain the submitted hash separately from the authoritative source hash, or retain an immutable submission snapshot/mismatch result sufficient for the later grade. Specify null and unavailable-source behavior and use the authoritative hash for staleness. Add a wrong-submitted-hash case that remains FAIL after restart; mirror entity, DTO, grade, and diagram changes.
